utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would you call the case, please, Mr. Registrar, in the ex parte hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. This is case IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor against Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm going to take the floor and address myself to Mr. Coric and his Defence counsel. As you know, pursuant to a problem that has arisen between Mr. Coric and his counsel, the Chamber had to make a ruling and appoint Mr. Jonjic for a period of two months, a temporary period, as Defence counsel. That two-month period expires on Monday, the 26th of June. In the meantime, Mr. Coric was invited to give us the names of your future Defence counsel on the Registrar's list, and we learnt that you came up with two names, and this procedure is still ongoing, because one of those lawyers, one of the counsel, has not yet sent in his documents, and the second Defence counsel will have to sit for an English-language test, which means that the Registrar is not able to make a decision today. On the other hand, the proceedings are continuing, and on Monday we're going to continue the sitting. We decided to convene this meeting so that you could state your views, Mr. Coric, on this issue. Perhaps there are some new elements that we're not aware of that have cropped up in the meantime, and I'm certain that you have contacted Counsel Jonjic in the meantime and that he probably made inquiries and dealt with your Defence case. Your lawyer also met us when we were in Bosnia-Herzegovina and told us about what befell you, so he acquitted himself affably as your counsel in your own interests. Those are the impressions that the three of us, us three Judges, gained. But as I said, perhaps there's some new elements that we should be made aware of that have cropped up in the meantime, and that is why we're very happy to hear your position from you, because you know that I always want to ensure that you have proper representation and fair representation. That is our objective always, fairness. And the three Judges have noted that up until now, your Defence counsel have acted in a very proper manner. Now, let us take the hypothesis of some lawyer being selected. This will all take time, because he will have to be brought up-to-date with the case and more than 10.000 documents and exhibits that there are in this case. So this -- there is the risk of prejudice, but otherwise everything was functioning perfectly well. So what I'd like to hear, Mr. Coric, is your line of thinking so that we as the Judges can be -- can make our ruling. I give you the floor. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. What I think is important for me to say today with respect to the questions you asked me is the following: Over the past two months, I established contact once again with Mr. Jonjic to a certain extent, but only in the space of those two months, and I never brought into question my decision and your ruling and decision that we should part, go our different ways after those two months have expired. After your decision, I sent in the Tribunal and the Trial Chamber the names of seven Zagreb lawyers. Two have made contact, and we need to have one of those two men selected for my Defence counsel. As far as I've been informed, that person sat for an English-language examination today and he has passed through all the other tests, and I was expecting to hear the results, what had happened, but I see that that is not the case today. I'm going to say something that I hadn't told anyone yet except for Mr. Jonjic. I am fully conscious that Mr. Jonjic, in the professional sense, worked well on the basis of the knowledge I had and what I was able to see both here in the courtroom and during the time we spent together working together, but I told Mr. Jonjic, unfortunately, I have some health problems that I'd like to address today. I take four tablets a day under the supervision of the physician of the Tribunal, three in the morning and a fourth pill in the afternoon. My contact with Mr. -- my contacts with Mr. Jonjic affect my blood pressure. It's very difficult for me to have to say that, but I must say it nonetheless. I don't wish him any ill-will but that is something that I'm not able to control, my reactions to him. Over the past few days, because of my father's death a while ago and my mother's death earlier on, I was under constant pressure and therefore under medical supervision, and my blood pressure has risen a great deal, and I sent in all the documentation, my medical records, to the physicians of the Tribunal. So it has reached a level where I ought to be hospitalised. The doctor told me two days after my father's death that the best thing would be for me to go to hospital, but I didn't want to go to hospital. I wanted to go home and attend the funeral. My health is poor today and there are days when I'm wondering whether to go to court or not. Now, to link that up to Mr. Jonjic, is perhaps a little -- or a little courageous -- or blunt and bold on my part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your blood pressure? How high? Did the doctor tell you how high is your blood pressure. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] My blood pressure is 180 over 120. So my diastolic is never under 120 despite the fact that I take four pills a day to lower my blood pressure. I can't do anything about that. I don't know if I am normal any more. I am under medical supervision, but what can I do? It seems to be my nature, and whenever I come into contact with Mr. Jonjic, my blood pressure seems to rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What does the doctor tell you? When you take your pills, does your blood pressure go down? What does the doctor tell you? Because I was not aware of the present state of affairs. So the doctor that examines you, is he optimistic with respect to your future health? THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] The last contact I had with my doctor was when he wanted to send me to hospital for a controlled examination, which was three days before the death of my father. I didn't go intentionally because I thought that if the situation became more complicated I wouldn't be allowed to go to my father's funeral. So he had -- he wanted to refer me to hospital because he said that the facilities in the Detention Unit weren't sufficient and that I would need to go to hospital. Now, I like to follow the old proverb that one knows what one -- what ails one best, so I'm trying to do the best I can to keep me up and running. But I told Mr. Jonjic of the situation some ten days ago when we met tete-a-tete. Were it not for this ex parte session, I wouldn't have told you that at all. So what happened between us, between myself and Mr. Jonjic, seems to make my health situation deteriorate, and I think that it -- my health is the most important for me. So everything else takes second place. What I want to do is to be able to come into court here and to see that my health is not impaired. The second point that I wanted to raise is this: When on the 21st I had direct contact with the Registry for the first time -- I won't take up too much of your time, but I would like to say this -- quite obviously those people made my position much more difficult and I have already stressed that. And it's only at the end of this two-month period of time that my next Defence counsel -- they waited for this two-month time limit to expire and still have not allowed me to select counsel. I'm going to keep quiet about that but quite obviously there's something afoot there, and if I think there's something devious afoot, I'll have to speak out. So I'd like to ask you to protect me from some people whom I think have quite different intentions when it comes to me. I'm asking you for assistance. People who are ready to join my team in Zagreb are following the proceedings of this trial on the internet. They have the documents that they have and receive documentation and material from various sides. They are ready to step on board, and I have helped them, I have done what I could for my part, so I'm -- I don't think that justice will be impaired in any way if after Monday I see new people here who will make up for lost time. And I'd like to have this main person came on board on the team, and then we can proceed according to the rules and regulations of this Tribunal. So please try and understand me and do what you can, and of course my action will depend on your decisions and rulings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Mr. Coric, I'm sure my colleagues will be asking you questions as well. Yes, you can sit down. No need to tire yourself standing up, as far as I'm concerned, but I do have a few questions to ask you. Please be seated. You've just told us that when you have a meeting with Mr. Jonjic your blood pressure rises. So you seem to be linking your state of health with the physical contact you have with your Defence counsel. That's what you have explained to me. And the conclusion on your part is that if you don't see Mr. Jonjic any more and have no further discussions with him, you think that your health will improve. Is that the summary of what you said? That is indeed what you told me, is it not? Very well. Now, my other concerns are your state of health, because you told us that the doctor wanted to refer you to hospital for treatment, so you will receive health care. It's not as -- you're not in a situation in the kind of situation that Slobodan Milosevic was in, who seemed to have the same sorts of problems as you. So if your doctor, the detention centre doctor, tells you that you have to go to hospital for examination, go. Have those medical examinations at the hospital. That seems to be necessary. So have the examinations done. The fact that you're in a detention centre doesn't mean that you shouldn't take care of your health. So that's the first point that I wish to raise you. But my concerns are these, and I'm sure my colleagues will intervene and have their own questions, but my concerns are that you are all -- are defended, that you have a Defence counsel in future. And as you can see, you see the quite considerable work that the Defence teams are having to get through with all the documents and every -- all the rest of it. So can you imagine that when one of these two men comes here and takes up the post of your Defence counsel, Mr. Jonjic can perhaps stay on for a few months in this interim period to facilitate the transition so that your new Defence counsel can be brought abreast of everything that is going on in the trial and be given assurances that the Defence counsel over a period of months can ensure that everything is done properly and that there is no prejudice against you. I don't know what my colleagues think, but I think I have a solution, and it is this: Either the Registrar should appoint or select one of these two people, the person that has just had his English examination, and that the person could come on board straight away and continue working with your present Defence counsel, Mr. Jonjic, for a number of months, let's say six months, and then after six months, if you're still in the same situation, then Mr. Jonjic will be obliged to step down and leave, and then the person who has replaced him will become lead counsel, and you'll have another lead counsel to defend you. So that is one solution that we can think about. What do you think about that solution? THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have thought about all these different variations, and to be quite frank, when you suggested that Mr. Jonjic stay for two months, had you said six months I wouldn't have minded. I thought relations would be a bit better. But after the experience that I have with everything, with all these matters -- and I told Mr. Jonjic this. We had a nice discussion, a calm discussion, and I said that I even felt better than when the two of us talk together rather than when I go back to my cell and then think over all the things we said and what we're doing and so on. So I'm now trying, even to my own detriment, to have a new period without Tomislav Jonjic, both in my mind, not to think about him, and not to have him at the trial. And I think that the person to replace him would be able to do so without any great detriment to me. So I would like to prevail upon you if we could do that as soon as possible. I talked to the Defence counsel. They are fully aware of the risks they would run. They're a little fearful of coming on board on this trial, given the scope of it, but we -- if you enable us to take that option and to have those people join us here as soon as possible to take over my Defence, then I think that would be the best solution. I will take on the responsibility myself. I'm willing to run the risk of having the people come in as soon as possible even if they're not ready and prepared enough, because this interim has been going on for two long. Let me just briefly repeat the main problem here: When you come into conflict with a friend, and I'm sure we've all done that, it's much worse than if you clash with somebody that you were -- you just had professional relationships with. Jonjic and I have had very close relations, both professional, political, family, friendly and so on, and suddenly it all fell through in the worst possible way, and I think that I was hit so hard by that that there's no medicament that can put it right. So both for my own good and for Tomislav himself, may we get -- have a solution to this problem and go forward with a new person, come what may. So please, could you try and help me and do as quickly as possible. Of course, if you have any more questions to ask, I'll be happy to answer them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues would like to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. [In English] Not asking a question, but I would also express my condolences to Mr. Coric for the loss, what his father's death meant for him. I would also like to say that after having listened to the President of our Trial Chamber and also having listened to Mr. Coric last time when this issue was discussed and also today, I do -- I do see the problems because sometimes even if the conflicts are not being brought to the public, at the same time I can understand that there are very personal, very private feelings which -- which are very difficult to explain, and especially when you mentioned that you are ill and you have your blood pressure very high, and it is indeed very high, then I have -- I would like to express my sympathy with you. On the other hand, there are certain issues which are really difficult for me also to understand. I also have followed with particular interest as a Judge and as a private person what has happened here during the hearings. I can also actually confirm what the President of the Trial Chamber already mentioned, that indeed the matter in Mr. Jonjic's position and his behaviour and professional knowledge also impressed me and I believe that he really did his best to represent you. So therefore, under these circumstances, I do not see too much other choice but to agree with the proposal which was made by the President -- by the Presiding Judge and to ask you to accept this as a provisional position and a provisional measure until and unless your choice will be then given to you and you can then work with your new Defence lawyer. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Part of Closed Session not made public by order of Trial Chamber] (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]. So I was quite impressed with your presentation today, and would also agree that we proceed as outlined by our Chamber Trial Chamber President. I would like to put into this a little additional viewpoint. You have stated today that the persons who are prepared to take over the Defence, and in the first place there's a lady who is about to pass her English test, have so far followed the trial and feel fully prepared, so that a transitory assistance by Mr. Jonjic, who I'd like to add as a footnote not only did his best, which is a bit a doubtful compliment, because someone who is not very good, if he does his best, the result is still not very good. But I would like to testify that Mr. Jonjic has done an excellent job by any standard. This is certainly an aside, and I think you do not yourself deny this. But whether your new counsel would be or will be prepared to do this, we would also have to hear from counsel. Our endeavour is to find the best solution for you and in marginal points at least, and this would be such a point, it would be our duty to make absolutely sure that where you feel safe, your new counsel also feels safe, and it's possible that perhaps Mr. Jonjic will, if he agrees, be retained as a consultant with no contact, as it were, and that could be a solution where one could combine the smooth entry into function of the new Defence team while taking care of your blood pressure. What would you think of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to add something, and we'll give you the floor back and then Mr. Jonjic will take the floor. So I think what you have understood, there's a consensus here on the part of all the Judges. The consensus would be like this: Mr. Jonjic would be appointed for a period of six months, and your counsel who is currently taking an English test - and we hope that this person has passed her test - would come on Monday already to represent you, and she would be the person whom you would be seeing. You will talk to her, you will see her in the Detention Unit, and you will work out your defence strategy with her. She will, of course, pass on to your -- her colleague all your instructions. So together with her, he will continue asking questions when it's time of the cross-examination. And he has done extremely well so far. So this would mean that you would have no physical contact, which according to you raises your blood pressure, but this would also be an advantage because this would also protect your interests. And third point, the new counsel that would be appointed, as you can see this is a very complex trial and there's -- there's -- there are a lot of common law aspects that need to be borne in mind, and the counsel that is appointed has to be operational straight away. So this is how I see things, the general picture, how things could work out for you. But it's for you, of course, to let us know what you feel about it. You have heard all three of us. I think we've been very clear. We've told you what our point of view is, and it's unusual that Judges agree on a particular topic. For once this is the case. I would like to know what your opinion is. I will give the floor to Mr. Jonjic afterwards, because he has to agree to all of this also. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have already told you what my standpoint is. I am, however, aware and conscious of all the arguments you have put forward here, and I thank you sincerely for helping me in this way. I feel that your intentions are the best possible. I have not spoken to the people who are preparing to enter my defence, and what you are proposing is new to me. I would need to discuss it with them, because they have already invested quite a lot of effort into this. I have to find out what they think of this proposal. I also need to know what Mr. Jonjic would be willing to accept, because he may refuse to accept working in such a team. I am not committing myself to anything but simply asking you to let me sleep on this, of course taking into account everything Your Honours have said, which is very reasonable and well-intentioned in view of what is best for myself and my co-accused, and therefore I would like to hear what Mr. Jonjic has to say and then to sleep on it. And also what kind of role he would be willing to play, if any, and what he thinks about all this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Jonjic, you have heard our point of view. You have heard what Mr. Coric has just said. And this could only work, of course, if you agree to it, because we know that you are a lawyer, you have your career to think of, and all of this might not be so easy for you. So what do you feel about it, and what's your view on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. First, I have to say that I am very embarrassed listening to people talking about me without being able to speak, but of course it was necessary to hear all this. Allow me to repeat very briefly the chronology of my relations with Mr. Coric, which he has described with great precision. We have known each other for some 23 years now, and we have been friends and very close until a conflict broke out between us in January of this year when Mr. Coric asked for my dismissal. I experienced a number of insults, some of them spoken out in this courtroom, but adhering to my code of professional ethics and later on the decision of the Chamber, I did my best to do my job professionally and in Mr. Coric's interest, even at times when we were not communicating at all. And this went on for several months. So of course I'm flattered when not only Your Honours but also Mr. Coric acknowledge that I have done my job professionally. Throughout this conflict, my position has been crystal clear. Regardless of the jurisprudence of this or any other Tribunal or court, I feel that in no court proceedings, especially proceedings as complex as these, can defence be adequately prepared if there is no trust between Defence counsel and accused. This is simply a sine qua non for a good defence. Mr. Coric, who is also no doubt aware of this, agreed very soon after the Pre-Trial Conference to have limited communication with me so that from the testimony of the first witness, Mrs. Drljevic, we communicated first in writing and then also orally and discussed defence strategy and questions to be put to witnesses. I am fully aware of the fact that my code of professional ethics still binds me today to act in the interests of my client even if it is something that I would not be inclined to do with respect to my feelings and inclinations, but there are several factors to be taken into account when making such a decision. I have fully prepared to hand over the entire case file on Monday, feeling that the decision had already been made. And let me remind Your Honours that I did ask to be relieved because I felt that Mr. Coric had the right to the kind of defence he wishes. It may not be the very best defence, even as it is not now the very best defence, but it has to be a defence that corresponds to his wishes and expectations. However, to go back to the proposal put forward here today, on the one hand I am fully aware of the fact that my primary obligation is to my client, Mr. Coric. In addition to this, however, I have obligations towards the members of my team. I don't know what the situation is with investigators, but I assume there would be no place for them, bearing in mind Mr. Coric's remarks. On the other hand, the colleagues or the people who will be part of the Defence in future are people I don't know personally. They have not contacted me. I don't know whether cooperation would be possible. And secondly, I am afraid that in the position proposed as an option by the Chamber would serve as a fig leaf for something that has nothing to do with law or justice. I must admit I'm a little bit taken aback by this proposal, and I would have to talk to Mr. Coric first of all, but it seems to me that I am being now put into the same kind of position I was in when I asked to be dismissed momentarily. If there is no trust between counsel and client, it cannot be replaced by any temporary measure. Thank you. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have heard what Mr. Jonjic has said and now things are quite clear to me. I suggest, if I may, that as of Monday, if the Registry, which I doubt, agrees, and I wish to reiterate my doubts concerning this entire process, the lead counsel for my new team, that the hand-over begin on Monday. The counsel -- the future counsel have already found accommodation and everything else in The Hague, and they are prepared to enter the courtroom the moment the Registry gives its approval. I have to say that the beginning of Mr. Jonjic's speech today has left an especially deep impression on me. Mr. Jonjic, let me say once again that it was you who dismissed me rather than the other way around. I told the Chamber this in writing. It was you who said to me, "Find another counsel." It wasn't the first time you had said that, but it was the first time I agreed to that, because I saw that I could no longer let you blackmail me. The second thing, which I find really hurtful, is that you organised several articles in the Croatian newspapers which have the highest circulation about me, and let me not go into this whole story again, but, Your Honours, please let's end this and part peacefully. That's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are not going to go into all of this from the beginning again. We are faced with the problem, and we have understood you well. We have listened to your lawyer. We shall withdraw for a few minutes to deliberate. If we can deliberate quickly, we will shall return to let you know what our oral decision is, and the Registry will then apply this instantly. So just wait for a few minutes and we will be back soon. We are well aware of this problem, as you can imagine. So we shall stand adjourned for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we resume our hearing, and the Chamber will render an oral decision, and at the end of the hearing we will ask the registrar to hand a copy of the transcript of this hearing to the Registry so that our decision can be implemented instantly. After having heard the explanations provided by Mr. Coric and having heard about his state of health, one team is ready and could take over already from Mr. Jonjic. The Trial Chamber, after having heard the explanation provided by Mr. Jonjic, the way he sees things and the fact that he cannot continue defending his client as there is no understanding between him and the accused, the Trial Chamber notes that this is the case and asks the Registrar to appoint as soon as possible the applicant who is currently taking an English test, and orders that until such a time that Mrs. Tomasevic is appointed, Mr. Jonjic continues in the meantime, which should be a short interval, continue to represent Mr. Coric so that Mr. Coric is currently represented and that there's nothing to prejudice his defence. The registrar will hand over a copy of the oral decision to the Registry of this Tribunal, who will very quickly appoint Mrs. Tomasevic, but if this cannot be done by Monday as our hearing is resuming on Monday, if this person can be here then, Mr. Jonjic will step down, and if this person can come in on Tuesday, then Mr. Jonjic will step down on Tuesday. If she comes on Wednesday, then he will step down on Wednesday. So we have tried to come up with an appropriate solution. You have your own reasons for not wanting to support this. And we have heard what Mr. Jonjic has had to say about all of this. Mr. Jonjic, so you may come back on Monday and hand over the case file to your colleague as soon as possible. I would like this to be recorded into the transcript of this trial. I speak in my own name, and I am sure my colleagues also agree to this: I do hope that the Registry will appoint you very quickly in another case so that you do not suffer from this and suffer no prejudice given the way things have evolved in these proceedings. You will then, of course, if you are appointed quickly again, be able to represent another client. You have in your capacity as a lawyer worked extremely well. I wanted this recorded in the transcript. Thank you. Mr. Coric, we shall meet again at a quarter past two on Monday and I hope that a solution will be found very quickly. The Court stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the ex parte hearing adjourned
